keyFindings.description:
drawDirective ends a line only at 
; micromark also ends one at a lone . Comment and message bodies are not line-feed normalized on the server (comment_create.go:339 normalizes only Suggestion.ReplaceWith; asks.go:327 normalizes only ask questions). Reproduced at the code head with the real server schema: 'Intro

:::abody:::

After' draws ':::abody:::' then 'body' then ':::' (text shown twice); ':::a:::'.repeat(3555) (31,995 chars, under the 32,000 cap) renders 44,245,530 characters in 1.5 s, quadratic. The default engine throws for the same input.

fitsContentRule returns true when a child matches a mark (remarkDispatchMarks wraps the blocks after a block-level in a dispatchMark), so the block stays typed and Milkdown drops it with its text. Reproduced: ':::ask # Heading words :::' renders one empty paragraph and logs 'Cannot create node for ask'. Breaks the architect's 'the read-only engine never drops text' rule and the PR body's claim.

The closing fence is any trailing colon run of the last source line, so a line that is not a fence is drawn as one: ':::note
body

[x]: mailto:' draws a ':' paragraph and '...[x]: https://e.x/a:::' draws ':::', though neither directive is closed. A closing fence is a line of only colons (three or more) after its container prefixes.

Lines 54-61 copy prosemirror-model's NodeType.createAndFill and the try/catch returns 'fits' on any throw; call type.createAndFill(defaultAttrs(type), placeholders) !== null and check target.isText instead of catching.
schema is optional only for one test; production always passes it, and without it the content-rule check is silently skipped. Make it required.
The readOnly option doc omits the content-rule case the transform also draws as text; the label predicate is duplicated at read-only-directives.ts:96 and :114.
